claude-s · music-video

Small things compound: a spoken-word lyric essay

Make a 20–30 s original spoken-word lyric film. Theme: small things compound, against deep time. Build it to a synthesised bed around 128 BPM: keys intro, a drop, a drums-out break before the turn, a louder final section, keys outro. Flat cel-shaded diagrams, a stat box counting up exponentially, karaoke captions with the held word in outline, hard cuts on the drops and crossfades everywhere else.

What the skill did

  • Wrote a 7-line original lyric, one line every 2 bars at 128 BPM. Chatterbox performed each line locally; align.py --spoken put each take's first word on its slot and timed every word with faster-whisper.
  • Karaoke captions fade each word on at its spoken onset. The word each line leans on (one, counting, billion, time, years, world, yet) is drawn as an outline.
  • A stat box counts live: cells double on every beat, then race from 2^8 to 2^30 and land on 1,073,741,824 as the word billion is spoken. Years and mountain height then climb together on a log axis (1 mm a year for 10 million years is 10 km).
  • Hard cuts only on the two drops, each with a 2-frame LUT stab; 2-frame crossfades everywhere else; every cut 50 ms before its downbeat.
  • One character in the same coat at three ages: a kid at the lens, an adult in the break, grey-haired at the lens again as the cell divides.
  • Checked by transcribing the finished mix: all 51 words heard in order; after each line's first word, onsets sit a median 14 ms from the karaoke, 91 % within 2 frames.

Sound

  • No SFX layer; the arrangement scores the picture: keys-only intro, a groove on the drop, 2 bars with drums and bass out while the picture pulses on each beat, the turn 3 dB louder, then keys to close.
  • Am7, Fmaj7, C/E, G, one chord a bar, all synthesised by sfx.py. Voice 6 dB over the bed with 2 dB of ducking, mastered to -14 LUFS and -1 dBTP.
